page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-224 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processors. It features 224 vCPUs mapped to 112 physical cores with multithreading enabled, alongside 224 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It lacks local NVMe storage and integrated GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, scoring in the top 10% on stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU tests, including physics and encryption workloads. Memory read-only small block cached bandwidth also ranks in the top 10%, reaching 13,016.92 GB/sec, while uncached large block read and write speeds remain strong. Single-core performance is strong, though multi-core compilation and ray tracing benchmarks show higher relative efficiency than standard single-threaded compression tasks. Redis SET operations perform exceptionally well, registering in the top 10% with 186.57 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is its low memory density of 1 GB per vCPU and the complete absence of local storage, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive databases or massive dataset caching. However, it offers high qualitative cost efficiency for compute-bound workloads that require massive parallel processing without high memory footprints. It is highly suited for parallel software compilation, ray tracing, static web serving, high-throughput Redis deployments, and prompt processing for smaller language models.
